rulings.ruling: Ruling: owner's reading; project retained. The only difference is a 2024 status of qualifying surviving spouse: the project counts the two spouse boxes only for married filing jointly or separately, the second also for qualifying surviving spouse. The worksheet does not say which statuses carry spouse boxes (i1040gi p. 90, State and Local Income Tax Refund Worksheet, line 6, "Check any boxes that apply"); the register's binding reading amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024 takes them from the standard deduction rules (p. 33, Line 12d, "If you or your spouse (if you are married and filing a joint return)"), under which a qualifying surviving spouse return has no spouse whose boxes it checks. Everywhere else the two agree: each box adds $1,550, or $1,950 for single or head of household, and the sum of per-box amounts equals the count times the amount.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 90, worksheet line 6: "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)" and footnote "*If your filing status is married filing separately, you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn’t filing a return, and can’t be claimed as a dependent on another person’s return"; p. 33, Line 12d: "Don’t check any boxes for your spouse if your filing status is head of household". executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/refund.json`; 1,382 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 640 partial records from 40 bases; 2,522 comparisons; every witness enumerated by an uncapped scratch rerun of tools/transcription/triage.mjs, the record keeps 6 per kind): 2,482 of 2,522 agree; 40 project-unknown (16 completed), all partial records withholding refund.status on no-refund bases. The candidate counts the spouse boxes only for a 2024 joint or separate return, as the project does (amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024), at $1,550 per box or $1,950 for single or head of household, and the sum of per-box amounts equals the count times the amount; the earlier qualifying-surviving-spouse difference is gone. The project reads the status before the boxes, the candidate only when a box is checked; line 6 is read only through line 7, and line 5 needs the 2024 status whenever line 7 is, so the difference is not reachable. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 90, worksheet line 6: "Multiply the number of boxes checked by $1,550 ($1,950 if your 2024 filing status was single or head of household)" and its footnote "*If your filing status is married filing separately, you can check the boxes for your spouse only if your spouse had no income, isn’t filing a return, and can’t be claimed as a dependent on another person’s return"; p. 33, Line 12d: "Don’t check any boxes for your spouse if your filing status is head of household". The candidate takes the spouse boxes for every 2024 filing status; the project counts them only for married filing jointly or separately, and zeroes them for single, head of household and qualifying surviving spouse (amb.2025.refund_boxes_2024). The candidate therefore needs the spouse answers where the source does not: stage16.mut.refund_single_unasked (single, a refund, the spouse questions unasked) gives the project $0.00 and the candidate unknown for refund.spouse_born. No value differs on any record. The completed-return candidate-unknown (spouse boxes withheld) and project-unknown (refund.status withheld where the candidate's answers are No) are partial records on bases with no refund: Every partial base of the bank is a return with no refund (refund.received $0.00), and s1.line1 reads the worksheet only when refund.has (refund.received more than zero) is true (forms/2025/s1.yaml), so the partial-record differences on those bases are on lines the return never reads. Triage executable-triage-v2 (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/refund.json`; 1,495 fixtures, 500 generated returns seed 20261026, 640 partial records from 40 bases; 2,635 comparisons): 2,514 agree; differences 81 candidate-unknown, 40 project-unknown; on completed returns 44 candidate-unknown, 22 project-unknown; every completed-return witness enumerated by an uncapped scratch rerun of the same evaluator (the record keeps 6 per kind). Project stands.
